# Sonner

Stacked toasts, from the Sonner library.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill odv-pill-out">Left out of Dense data</span> Dense data already has its own toast to confirm a saved change. A second toast would add a part. A small team keeps fewer parts right. <span class="odv-instead">Use instead: <a href="./toast">Toast</a>, <a href="./alert">Alert</a></span></p>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Many short confirmations that may arrive close together.
- **Not when:** A message people must read or act on (alert or dialog).

Instead:

- [Toast](./toast.md): Open DS's own single toast.
- [Alert](./alert.md): A message that stays.

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] Toasts are announced politely and do not take focus. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add sonner
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Sonner sets no colours, corners or shadows of its own; it takes them from the components inside it.
